title: Evaporated Milk vs Condensed Milk: Why They Are Not Interchangeable

seo.title: Evaporated Milk vs Condensed Milk
seo.meta_description: Evaporated milk is concentrated unsweetened milk; sweetened condensed milk can contain roughly 50–55 g of sugars and more than 320 calories per 100 g.
seo.search_intent: Distinguish evaporated and condensed milk by sugar, calories, texture, and culinary use.

excerpt: Evaporated milk is concentrated milk without the huge added-sugar load of sweetened condensed milk. Condensed milk can contain roughly 50–55 g of sugars per 100 g, making it much sweeter, thicker, and more calorie-dense.
content_html:
Both products start by removing water from milk, but that shared beginning hides a major difference. Evaporated milk is concentrated unsweetened milk; sweetened condensed milk adds enough sugar to become a dessert ingredient rather than a simple milk substitute.

The sugar gap is enormous

Typical evaporated whole milk provides roughly 130–140 calories and about 10–12 g of naturally occurring sugars per 100 g. Sweetened condensed milk can exceed 320 calories and contain roughly 50–55 g of sugars per 100 g.

That is why their jobs in recipes differ

Evaporated milk adds dairy body to soups, sauces, casseroles, and desserts without making them intensely sweet. Condensed milk delivers both concentrated dairy solids and sugar, which is useful in pies, candies, coffee drinks, and no-churn desserts.

Condensed milk is much more viscous

The high sugar concentration binds water and creates the thick, glossy texture associated with condensed milk. Evaporated milk is richer than regular milk, but it still pours much more freely.

Can one replace the other?

Not cup for cup without reformulating the recipe. Replacing condensed milk with evaporated milk removes a large amount of sugar and solids; replacing evaporated milk with condensed milk makes a savory or lightly sweet recipe far too sweet.

The label shortcut

Think “water removed” for evaporated milk and “water removed plus a lot of sugar” for sweetened condensed milk. That difference changes calories, sweetness, texture, and culinary use.

faq.question: Is evaporated milk sweet?
faq.answer: It contains natural milk sugar, but it is not intensely sweet like sweetened condensed milk.

faq.question: Which has more calories?
faq.answer: Sweetened condensed milk, largely because of its high added-sugar content.

faq.question: Can I substitute them 1:1?
faq.answer: Usually not. Their sugar concentration and texture are too different for a direct swap.
